 Cyclone 'Akvan' LIVE updates: Over one lakh evacuated in Odisha as landfall likely near Gopalpur; red alert for three A.P. districts
 The IMD says the corridor for landfall, likely on Nov. 20 noon, stretches from Andhra's Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh to Odisha's Puri
 Updated - November 19, 2026 02:55 pm IST 
 The Hindu Bureau READ LATER 
 SEE ALL 
 Remove 
 The projected trajectory of the Severe Cyclonic Storm (SCS) Akvan kept changing its path on November 18, 2026, due to which the northern parts of Andhra Pradesh and southern parts of Odisha were placed on alert.
 | Photo Credit: 
 K.R. Deepak
 Severe cyclonic storm ‘Akvan’ continues to moved northward as of Thursday morning (November 19, 2026) at a speed of 12 kmph over the westcentral Bay of Bengal, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said. After a day of uncertainty that kept cyclone forecasters puzzled, the new projected track of severe cyclonic storm Akvan points to a probable landfall on the Odisha coast, near Gopalpur, by November 20 noon. 
 Also read | Cyclone Akvan shifts track again 
 However, IMD experts at Amaravati feel there is a slight possibility of the system changing its track and making landfall near the extreme end of north coastal Andhra Pradesh. The IMD continues to say that the landfall corridor stretches from Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh to Puri in Odisha. The impact of the cyclone on Andhra Pradesh has lessened, but vigil is being maintained, since north coastal Andhra Pradesh has been put on an extremely heavy rainfall alert.
 Read More : Why is Bay of Bengal so active? Expert explains | Cyclone Akvan 
 Odisha on Thursday (November 19, 2026) stepped up evacuation of people, positioning of disaster response forces and emptying of reservoirs in southern and coastal districts. Office of Special Relief Commissioner said more than one lakh people, including close to 10,000 pregnant women, have been shifted to safer places. While Ganjam district under which Gopalpur lies alone has shifted over 50,000 people, Gajapati and Kandhamal districts have relocated 16,000 and 3000 people respectively.
 Railway authorities have rescheduled three trains so far. Andhra Pradesh is experiencing a very rare event, since it is not often that a State sees three tropical cyclones crossing its coast within a month, said IMD Director General of Meteorology.

 November 19, 2026 14:55 Severe Cyclonic Storm 'Akvan' continues to move northwards at 17 kmph Severe cyclonic storm ‘Akvan’ continues to move northwards with a speed of 17 kmph, the IMD said in its latest update on Thursday afternoon (November 19, 2026).
 It is likely to move north-northwestward and cross North Andhra Pradesh & Yanam and South Odisha coasts between Narsapur and Puri, close to Gopalpur, by noon of 20th November, 2026 with the maximum sustained wind speed of 90-100 kmph gusting to 110 kmph, it added.
 November 19, 2026 14:20 Andhra's Srikakulam, Vizianagaram on high alert The Srikakulam and Vizianagaram district administrations are on high alert ahead of Cyclone Akvan, which is expected to cross the coast near Gopalpur in Odisha on Friday (November 20, 2026). Srikakulam, which suffered heavily in the two recent cyclones, Arnab and Murasu , is ready to face the new challenge.
 Srikakulam Collector Swapnil Dinakar Pundkar and other officials visited Donkuru and other villages of Ichchapuram , on the Andhra Pradesh-Odisha border, to review the preparedness of local officials. Ichchapuram, Sompeta and other areas were badly affected by floods in the Bahuda after the earlier cyclones.
 Vizianagaram Collector S. Ramsundar Reddy reviewed the situation at the coastal villages of Pusapatirega and Bhogapuram and asked officials to take necessary measures ahead of the cyclone. He said fishermen had been advised not to venture into the sea for the next few days on the government’s orders.
 The Hindu Bureau 
 November 19, 2026 13:58 Cyclone 'Akvan': IMD forecasts heavy rain in south Bengal till Nov. 21 The IMD on Thursday (November 19, 2026) forecast heavy rain in the southern districts of West Bengal in the next two days as cyclonic storm ‘Akvan’ approaches the east coast.
 Kolkata and other southern districts of the state experienced overnight rain as a result of the weather system, it said.
 The coastal districts of South 24 Parganas and Purba Medinipur, along with Kolkata, Howrah and Paschim Medinipur, received overnight rain due to the weather conditions, it said.
 Heavy rain is likely over North 24 Parganas, Paschim Medinipur, Jhargram and Bankura, the IMD said.
 Thunderstorms, accompanied by gusty winds reaching speeds of 30-40 kmph, will occur over Kolkata and other south Bengal districts till Saturday, it said. The Met office advised fishermen not to venture into the sea till Saturday (November 21, 2026), as conditions will be rough owing to the severe cyclonic storm over the Bay of Bengal.
 PTI 
 November 19, 2026 13:44 Cyclone ‘Akvan’ heads for Odisha; over one lakh people evacuated Odisha on Thursday (November 19, 2026) stepped up evacuation of people, positioning of disaster response forces and emptying of reservoirs in southern and coastal districts as the Severe Cyclonic Storm ‘Akvan’ is expected cross the State’s coast, close to east of Gopalpur, by noon of November 20.
 Office of Special Relief Commissioner said more than one lakh people, including close to 10,000 pregnant women, have been shifted to safer places. While Ganjam district under which Gopalpur lies alone has shifted over 50,000 people, Gajapati and Kandhamal districts have relocated 16,000 and 3000 people respectively.
 Meanwhile, the State government also closed tourist sites including Chilika Lake, Puri beaches, Bhitarakanika and Nandankanan Zoological Park.
 Cyclone ‘Akvan’ heads for Odisha; over one lakh people evacuated
 Odisha evacuates over 100k as Severe Cyclonic Storm Akvan nears coast, closing tourist sites and schools, with rescue prep underway.
 November 19, 2026 13:09 Cyclone Akvan to spare most of Andhra; red alert remains for three districts Severe cyclonic storm Akvan may not have much impact on Andhra Pradesh , since the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has revised its initial forecast and said isolated extremely heavy rainfall (red alert) is likely only in three districts, Srikakulam, Vizianagaram and Parvathipuram Manyam, on Thursday (November 19, 2026).
 Earlier, Visakhapatnam , Anakapalli, Alluri Sitharama Raju and Kakinada were also put on red alert. They have now been put on orange alert for November 19. There are no red alerts for the State on November 20, when the system is likely to cross the coast near Gopalpur in Odisha . But there is an orange alert for Srikakulam and Parvathipuram Manyam on November 20, since isolated very heavy rainfall is likely.

 Cyclone Akvan: red alert only for Srikakulam, Vizianagaram and Parvathipuram Manyam on November 19 as the storm heads for landfall near Gopalpur in Odisha.
 November 19, 2026 12:53 Cyclone Akvan: 80 Andhra fishermen stranded at Odisha jetty Around 80 fishermen from Andhra Pradesh’s Kakinada, along with 10 motorised boats, have taken shelter in Odisha’s Ganjam district as rough sea conditions under the influence of severe cyclonic storm Akvan prevented them from returning home, officials said on Thursday (November 19, 2026).
 The fishermen were out in the deep sea when worsening weather conditions forced them to take shelter at the fish landing centre in Aryapalli, Assistant Fisheries Officer (Marine) Devidutt Mohanty said.
 The Ganjam district administration has provided them with necessary facilities at the jetty, he said. They have food supplies on their boats and are preparing their own meals, adding that they would return to Andhra Pradesh once sea conditions improve.
 PTI 
 November 19, 2026 12:35 Odisha evacuates over 80,000 people, deploys 74 rescue teams The Odisha government has evacuated more than 80,000 people to safety, deployed 74 rescue teams and closed educational institutes in several districts as precautionary measures in view of Cyclone ‘Akvan’, officials said.
 The State government has closed educational institutes in districts marked under ‘red’ (take action), ‘orange’ (be prepared) and ‘yellow’ (be aware) warnings, another official said, adding that 74 rescue teams have been deployed in Malkangiri, Koraput, Rayagada, Kalahandi, Gajapati, Ganjam, Kandhamal, Boudh, Puri, Nayagarh and Khurda districts.
 As Ganjam is likely to be the worst hit by the impending cyclone, the district administration has shifted 36,398 people to shelters by 6 a.m. on Thursday (November 19, 2026), and evacuation is underway, an official said.
 Altogether, 308 shelters are operational, with free kitchens serving the evacuated people, he said, adding that 1,098 pregnant women have been shifted safely.
 PTI 
 November 19, 2026 12:30 Cyclone 'Akvan' to trigger heavy rain in parts of Jharkhand Cyclone ‘Akvan’, which is expected to make landfall between Narsapur in northern Andhra Pradesh and Odisha’s Puri on Friday afternoon (November 20, 2026), is likely to bring heavy rainfall to parts of Jharkhand over two to three days, an IMD official said.
 The impact of the system could be felt in southern and central parts of the state from Thursday evening with sporadic spells of light rain, he said.
 “A yellow alert (to be updated) of heavy rainfall has been issued for 11 Jharkhand districts on Friday. The same alert has also been issued for eight districts on Saturday,” Ranchi Meteorological Centre’s Deputy Director Abhishek Anand said.
 The districts, likely to experience heavy rainfall for 24 hours from 8.30 a.m. on Friday (November 20, 2026), include Lohardaga, Gumla, Simdega, Ramgarh, Ranchi, Khunti, Bokaro, Dhanbad, Saraikela-Kharsawan, West and East Singhbhum.
 PTI 
 November 19, 2026 11:57 What weather experts say on the revised landfall point of cyclone Akvan After a day of uncertainty that kept cyclone forecasters puzzled, the new projected track of ​ severe cyclonic storm Akvan ​ points to a probable landfall on the ​ Odisha ​ coast, near Gopalpur.
 However, weather experts at the India Meteorological Department (IMD), Amaravati, feel there is a slight possibility of the system changing its track and making landfall near the extreme end of north coastal Andhra Pradesh. The IMD continues to say that the landfall corridor stretches from Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh to Puri in Odisha. The impact of the cyclone on ​ Andhra Pradesh ​ has lessened, but vigil is being maintained, since north coastal Andhra Pradesh has been put on an extremely heavy rainfall alert.
 The system was initially thought to cross the central Andhra Pradesh coast, near Bapatla and Krishna districts. But its trajectory has changed constantly since cyclogenesis, said P.L.N. Murthy, Head of the Cyclone Warning Centre, Visakhapatnam.
 ​ Cyclone Akvan now likely to cross coast near Gopalpur in Odisha; north Andhra stays on alert
 Cyclone Akvan is now likely to cross the coast near Gopalpur in Odisha by Friday noon with winds of up to 110 kmph; north coastal Andhra stays on rain alert.
 ​
 November 19, 2026 11:38 Odisha govt. evacuates nearly 50,000 people; highest from Ganjam Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi said around 50,000 people have so far been evacuated to safety ahead of the likely landfall of severe cyclonic storm ‘Akvan’ between Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh and Puri in the eastern State.
 Highest number of people will be evacuated from Ganjam district and the process was underway, he added.
 People were being shifted to safer locations from several villages of Ganjam, Gajapati, Kandhamal, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri districts, the CM said.
 The State government has set up 3,000 cyclone shelters, of which 448 were already operational, Mr. Majhi said.
 Odisha has allocated ₹20 crore to 15 districts to carry out relief and rescue operations.
 PTI 
 November 19, 2026 11:23 Cyclone Akvan: Three trains rescheduled Railways authorities have rescheduled three trains in view of cyclone Akvan.
 Train No. 18046 Charlapalli-Shalimar East Coast Express, scheduled to depart at 08:40 hours on Thursday, November 19, has been rescheduled to depart at 15:40 hours on the same day due to the cyclone.
 Similarly, Train No.12704 Secunderabad-Howrah Falaknuma Express, scheduled to depart at 15:55 hours on November 19, will now depart at 17:55 hours.
 Train No.15227 SMVT Bengaluru-Muzaffarpur Express, scheduled to depart at 00:30 hours on Thursday, has also been rescheduled to depart at 08:30 hours on the same day.
 ANI 
 November 19, 2026 11:21 Tamil Nadu may have to wait till November 23 for heavy rain With the severe cyclonic storm climbing further north, chances for a widespread or intense rainfall over Tamil Nadu have diminished further. The Regional Meteorological Centre has forecast isolated light rainfall to continue over ghat areas of Western Ghats districts till November 21. One or two places in north coastal Tamil Nadu may get mild rainfall on November 21.
 While moderate rainfall has been forecast for parts of coastal Tamil Nadu on November 22, Northeast monsoon is likely to return to active phase over Tamil Nadu with fairly widespread rainfall from November 23.
 Heavy rainfall is likely to occur over 14 delta and south Tamil Nadu districts, including Thanjavur, Theni and Kanniyakumari districts on November 23. North TN districts, including Chennai and Ranipet, too would receive moderate rainfall till November 24.

 Cyclone Akvan shifts track again; heavy rain in Tamil Nadu now forecast for November 23 amid multiple forecast revisions by IMD.
 November 19, 2026 11:17 Cyclone Akvan moves northwards, landfall likely near Gopalpur by Nov. 20 noon Severe cyclonic storm ‘Akvan’ continues to moved northward as of Thursday morning (November 19, 2026) at a speed of 12 kmph over the westcentral Bay of Bengal, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said. It is likely to move north-northwestwards and cross the Andhra-Odisha coasts between Narsapur and Puri, close to the east of Gopalpur, by November 20 noon. The storm is expected to make landfall with maximum sustained wind speeds of 90-100 kmph, gusting to 110 kmph, the IMD added.
 November 19, 2026 11:15 Uncertainty over path of Cyclone Akvan; North A.P. and South Odisha on alert The projected trajectory of the Severe Cyclonic Storm (SCS) Akvan kept changing its path on Wednesday (November 18, 2026). And, due to the uncertainty over the movement of the system, the northern parts of Andhra Pradesh and southern parts of Odisha have now been placed on alert.
 While the initial forecast of the India Meteorological Department (IMD) showed that the system may move towards Machilipatnam, or Bapatla of Central Andhra Pradesh as a Very Severe Cyclonic Storm (VSCS), a revised forecast said Akvan may not intensify into a VSCS, and its trajectory also changed later to Narsapur-Kakinada, and then further north towards North Andhra and South Odisha.
